title: Occupation of Sirhind And Slaughter of Nawab Zain Khan

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing the news about (the rising power of the Sikhs), The Gilja Pathans dispatched four Tumans2 of troops. Hearing the rumours about Ahmed Shah Abdali's approach, All the Singh Misls also gathered together at one place. (1)
lines: Hearing the news about (the rising power of the Sikhs),
The Gilja Pathans dispatched four Tumans2 of troops.
Hearing the rumours about Ahmed Shah Abdali's approach,
All the Singh Misls also gathered together at one place.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The four Pathan brigades positioning themselves at four corners, Landed at the four cities of Sirhind, Multan, Sialkot and Lahore. All the Singh contingents proceeding in one direction, Converged in a single formation at the city of Sirhind. (2)
lines: The four Pathan brigades positioning themselves at four corners,
Landed at the four cities of Sirhind,
Multan,
Sialkot and Lahore.
All the Singh contingents proceeding in one direction,
Converged in a single formation at the city of Sirhind.

blocks.text: Gathering intelligence about Sirhind from a distance, The Singhs learnt that it was unguarded at that moment.
That its custodian had proceeded on a revenue collection spree, The same news had traveled to the gathered Singhs. (3)
lines: That its custodian had proceeded on a revenue collection spree,
The same news had traveled to the gathered Singhs.

blocks.text: Hearing this news, the Singhs rushed in from far and wide, Even as a few of Nawab's informers were also around in the area. As these informers informed the Nawab about the Singhs' movement, Zain Khan, the Sirhind Nawab, also returned towards Sirhind. (4)
lines: Hearing this news, the Singhs rushed in from far and wide,
Even as a few of Nawab's informers were also around in the area.
As these informers informed the Nawab about the Singhs' movement,
Zain Khan, the Sirhind Nawab, also returned towards Sirhind.

blocks.text: Thereupon, did the Khalsa Panth pass a resolution; Let them, first of all, do away with Nawab Zain Khan, Now that this swine of a Nawab had come out in the open, Let him be done away with before he finds a safe sanctuary. (5)
lines: Thereupon, did the Khalsa Panth pass a resolution;
Let them, first of all, do away with Nawab Zain Khan,
Now that this swine of a Nawab had come out in the open,
Let him be done away with before he finds a safe sanctuary.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The same strategy did the Khalsa Panth adopt, Positioning themselves on the other side of Sirhind. Zain Khan's passage did they stand to block, After deliberating thoroughly all the pros and cons. (6)
lines: The same strategy did the Khalsa Panth adopt,
Positioning themselves on the other side of Sirhind.
Zain Khan's passage did they stand to block,
After deliberating thoroughly all the pros and cons.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Zain Khan, too, did get this information, That the Singhs (contenders for power) had blocked his passage. Much did he think and grieve over his predicament, Would that he had not come out of Sirbind! (7)
lines: Zain Khan, too, did get this information,
That the Singhs (contenders for power) had blocked his passage.
Much did he think and grieve over his predicament,
Would that he had not come out of Sirbind!

blocks.text: Hardly could he think of a place to rush in and be safe, As moment of imminent death had indeed arrived. Speedily did he rush towards the city of Sirhind, Even as the Singhs had positioned themselves on both sides. (8)
lines: Hardly could he think of a place to rush in and be safe,
As moment of imminent death had indeed arrived.
Speedily did he rush towards the city of Sirhind,
Even as the Singhs had positioned themselves on both sides.

blocks.text: At Bhanganpur3 had the Buddha Dal4 Singhs put up a camp, At village Panjowal5 had the Taruna Dal6 Singhs camped. At village Nanhera7 did Zain Khan put up a camp, Like a rabbit indeed was he hiding in the wild growth. (9)
lines: At Bhanganpur3 had the Buddha Dal4 Singhs put up a camp,
At village Panjowal5 had the Taruna Dal6 Singhs camped.
At village Nanhera7 did Zain Khan put up a camp,
Like a rabbit indeed was he hiding in the wild growth.

blocks.text: Throughout the night did the Singhs keep a vigil, Lest Zain Khan should sneak into the cursed city8 . Zain Khan, too, kept awake throughout the night, As he prepared to move out in the early hours. (10)
lines: Throughout the night did the Singhs keep a vigil,
Lest Zain Khan should sneak into the cursed city8 .
Zain Khan, too, kept awake throughout the night,
As he prepared to move out in the early hours.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Heavy artillery guns, medium guns and long-barreled guns, Did Zain Khan carry with his moving contingents. Thinking that these fire arms would hold the Khalsa back, Such a strategy did he decide (to seek his escape). (11)
lines: Heavy artillery guns, medium guns and long-barreled guns,
Did Zain Khan carry with his moving contingents.
Thinking that these fire arms would hold the Khalsa back,
Such a strategy did he decide (to seek his escape).

blocks.text: Chaupai:
Silently thus did he make a move, Keeping all his war drums in the rear guard. He asked his standard bearers not to beat these drums, So that the Singhs might not advance towards him. (12)
lines: Silently thus did he make a move,
Keeping all his war drums in the rear guard.
He asked his standard bearers not to beat these drums,
So that the Singhs might not advance towards him.

blocks.text: The Singh contingent which consisted of Majhail9 Singhs, Desperate did they get to pick up a fight. Listen to the account of the Buddha Dal contingent, Who, too, had deployed informers during that night. (13)
lines: The Singh contingent which consisted of Majhail9 Singhs,
Desperate did they get to pick up a fight.
Listen to the account of the Buddha Dal contingent,
Who, too, had deployed informers during that night.

blocks.text: As these informers gave information about Zain Khan's move, Many a Singh rushed out as they heard the news. Incidentally as both the Singh contingents arrived together, Much noise did they make with their musket fires. (14)
lines: As these informers gave information about Zain Khan's move,
Many a Singh rushed out as they heard the news.
Incidentally as both the Singh contingents arrived together,
Much noise did they make with their musket fires.

blocks.text: As more Singhs arrived after hearing the bullet fires, They could not stop the march of Pathan forces. Desperately did the Pathans wish to enter Sirhind, Then alone would they be able to save their lives. (15)
lines: As more Singhs arrived after hearing the bullet fires,
They could not stop the march of Pathan forces.
Desperately did the Pathans wish to enter Sirhind,
Then alone would they be able to save their lives.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Must Zain Khan be killed outside the city, Thus did the Singhs wish so desperately. Never could he fall into their hands, Once he succeeded in entering the city of Sirhind. (16)
lines: Must Zain Khan be killed outside the city,
Thus did the Singhs wish so desperately.
Never could he fall into their hands,
Once he succeeded in entering the city of Sirhind.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Slaughter of Singhs was indeed he in Singhs' estimation, For the great massacre of Singhs was he responsible. Must the Singhs settle their scores with him, Must they burry him in the grave there and then. (17)
lines: Slaughter of Singhs was indeed he in Singhs' estimation,
For the great massacre of Singhs was he responsible.
Must the Singhs settle their scores with him,
Must they burry him in the grave there and then.

blocks.text: The Singhs, being extremely sick of Zain Khan's atrocities, They pounced upon him as a bird of prey pounces upon its prey. Zain Khan, changing many strategies and making many moves, He did not take a permanent position to fight the Singhs. (18)
lines: The Singhs, being extremely sick of Zain Khan's atrocities,
They pounced upon him as a bird of prey pounces upon its prey.
Zain Khan, changing many strategies and making many moves,
He did not take a permanent position to fight the Singhs.

blocks.text: Deploying a part of his force to engage the Singhs, He himself made a move towards the city of Sirhind. Facing a volley of bullets by Singhs from the front, He was humbled by these terrible gun fires. (19)
lines: Deploying a part of his force to engage the Singhs,
He himself made a move towards the city of Sirhind.
Facing a volley of bullets by Singhs from the front,
He was humbled by these terrible gun fires.

blocks.text: Whosoever became a target of the Singhs' firearms attack, How could he escape without being hit by it? Singhs being ace shooters and expert sword wielders, How could the Singhs' mission be not fulfilled? (20)
lines: Whosoever became a target of the Singhs' firearms attack,
How could he escape without being hit by it?
Singhs being ace shooters and expert sword wielders,
How could the Singhs' mission be not fulfilled?

blocks.text: Dohra:

As the Khalsa Panth Singhs opened a volley of fire, The Gilja Pathan (Zain Khan) came directly under its range. As a bullet pierced through his lower intestines, To the ground did he fall with a rebound. (21)
lines: As the Khalsa Panth Singhs opened a volley of fire,
The Gilja Pathan (Zain Khan) came directly under its range.
As a bullet pierced through his lower intestines,
To the ground did he fall with a rebound.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Much hue and cry did the Pathan troops raise at his fall, With cries of Barkun! Barkun!10 They rushed to pick him up. From the sound of their cries did the Singhs come to know, The location where wounded Zain Khan had fallen. (22)
lines: Much hue and cry did the Pathan troops raise at his fall,
With cries of Barkun!
Barkun!10 They rushed to pick him up.
From the sound of their cries did the Singhs come to know,
The location where wounded Zain Khan had fallen.

blocks.text: Thereupon, as a large number of Singhs converged on the spot, The Gilja Pathans vanished leaving behind Zain Khan's dead body. The Singhs kept killing the Pathans wherever they moved, The Pathans kept on laying down the arms pleading for mercy. (23)
lines: Thereupon, as a large number of Singhs converged on the spot,
The Gilja Pathans vanished leaving behind Zain Khan's dead body.
The Singhs kept killing the Pathans wherever they moved,
The Pathans kept on laying down the arms pleading for mercy.

blocks.text: Whosoever laid down his arms before the Singhs, Him the Singhs did not attack and kill. Singhs, being apostles of compassion at heart, Why should they take revenge from the defenceless? (24)
lines: Whosoever laid down his arms before the Singhs,
Him the Singhs did not attack and kill.
Singhs, being apostles of compassion at heart,
Why should they take revenge from the defenceless?

blocks.text: Pathan horses and camels beng loaded with treasures and weapons, Instantly prosperous did the Singhs become by robbing them off. Both factions of the Singhs felt delighted after robbing Pathans, As life-long poverty of some of them was wiped off forever. (25)
lines: Pathan horses and camels beng loaded with treasures and weapons,
Instantly prosperous did the Singhs become by robbing them off.
Both factions of the Singhs felt delighted after robbing Pathans,
As life-long poverty of some of them was wiped off forever.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Huge camels loaded with merchandise there were, Loaded and mounted were the artillery guns there. Whosoever came across these treasures and weapons, Quietly did they take these valuables in their possession. (26)
lines: Huge camels loaded with merchandise there were,
Loaded and mounted were the artillery guns there.
Whosoever came across these treasures and weapons,
Quietly did they take these valuables in their possession.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

It was in the year Eighteen hundred and twenty" , As per the calendar named after king Vikramaditya. It was the fourth of Magh12 , four miles from Sirhind, That Zain Khan was slaughtered near Pir Jain13 . (27)
lines: It was in the year Eighteen hundred and twenty" ,
As per the calendar named after king Vikramaditya.
It was the fourth of Magh12 , four miles from Sirhind,
That Zain Khan was slaughtered near Pir Jain13 .
